proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Assume \(s=\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\). Determine whether the proved bracket can be sharpened to \(\rho_\star(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\) over \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Any converse must use priors on observed laws in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) whose full-law null lifts in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm F}\) each have constant \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\) and exact \(X\sim\lambda\), while preserving all separate Hölder restrictions. Determine whether the sharp rough-regime rate depends on \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) separately and whether logarithms occur at any additional boundary or interior elbow within this strict regime. proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original question asks for an all-phase exact frontier, but the proved bracket closes the entire no-penalty region, including equality, while no legal same-class nuisance-scale converse is known in the strict rough regime. Narrowing localizes the research question to precisely the unresolved mathematics and does not alter the model class.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For \(\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), whether the nuisance-limited upper endpoint \(r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\) is the full-class minimax separation rate, and whether any further rough-regime elbow carries a logarithmic factor.
open_obligations.obstruction: The oracle Bernoulli bump mixture proves only the oracle lower endpoint. A nuisance-scale converse requires a prior whose every null draw has constant CATE, whose alternatives satisfy the separate propensity, baseline, and CATE Hölder restrictions, and whose complete four-cell observed likelihood remains close under exact uniform design. The available correlated propensity--baseline perturbation does not control all transition regions and can force the alternative baseline to inherit impermissible CATE roughness when \(\beta>\gamma\).
open_obligations.attempted: The corrected projection upper bound was audited for unrelated ranks, including regimes with both ranks larger than \(n\), and the oracle sign-mixture lower bound was completed. A local moment-matched propensity--baseline perturbation was not promoted because it neither matches the full observed Bernoulli cell likelihood nor bounds the fixed-design transition-region contribution.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Within \(\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), the exact minimax phase map, any separate dependence on \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), any logarithmic factors at further elbows, and strict inclusion or non-inclusion relations with the Yu and Dhawan--Guo--Shah applicability classes.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact phase map depends on the unresolved nuisance-scale observational converse. In addition, a bump pack can be orthogonalized against one fixed direction, but the hunted direction is training-sample random, and the published regularity predicates contain learner, variance, boundary, nondegeneracy, and moment conditions not implied by membership in the frozen observed-law class.
open_obligations.attempted: The achieved upper-envelope boundary was derived algebraically; the Dhawan--Guo--Shah score, energy, conditional correlation requirement, and signal requirement were separated; and Yu's learner and root-\(n\) signal requirements were separated. No sequence was certified to satisfy every relevant published applicability condition while also proving the requested strict relation.

prose_updates.tldr: For constant-CATE testing over the exact observed-data image of the bounded causal Hölder class, the strongest proved result is the full-class bracket \(c_{\mathrm{rate}}r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\le\rho_\star(n)\le C_{\mathrm{rate}}\{r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\vee r_{\mathrm{nu}}(n)\}\). The endpoints coincide exactly when \(\alpha+\beta\ge2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), including equality without a logarithmic loss, so rough confounding has no minimax-rate penalty throughout that region. The upper endpoint is attained by an explicit, terminating, uniformly calibrated higher-order corrected-energy test with deterministic tuning. Only the strict complementary regime remains open: whether \(r_{\mathrm{nu}}\) is sharp, whether \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) create separate elbows, and whether further rough-regime boundaries carry logarithms. Yu (2026) and Dhawan--Guo--Shah (2026) are procedure-level power comparators under additional learner, direction, variance, and regularity conditions, not uniform full-class minimax comparators.

project_justification.gap: The missing result is no longer an all-phase frontier: the bracket and exact no-penalty phase are proved. The remaining gap is a legal same-class observational converse in the strict rough regime \(\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), where no established construction simultaneously keeps every null CATE constant, preserves the separate Hölder restrictions, maintains exact uniform design, and controls the complete observed likelihood. Existing CATE-estimation and rough-mean heteroskedasticity results do not supply that converse for this experiment.
project_justification.niche: The note isolates continuous-design constancy testing for a CATE through the variance separation \(V(P)\), under exact uniform design, bounded observed outcomes, overlap, and separate Hölder geometry for the propensity, baseline, and effect. This differs from scalar-ATE estimation in a discrete arbitrary-cell-mass experiment and from first-order testing guarantees that assume fitted-learner rates, favorable directions, or conditional variance conditions.
project_justification.fill: The contribution is a proved two-sided full-class bracket, an exact oracle/no-penalty phase including its equality case without logarithmic loss, and a data-computable higher-order corrected-energy test attaining the upper endpoint with deterministic class-based tuning and finite arithmetic complexity. The unresolved program is explicitly restricted to sharpness and finer phase structure below the no-penalty boundary; no extra model or estimator-side premise is added to manufacture a match.

prose_updates.related_work: The closest accepted local comparator is \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier/v1}\), \(\texttt{thm:two-sided-minimax-bracket-all-d}\). It estimates a scalar ATE in a discrete arbitrary-cell-mass experiment with a known heterogeneity radius and rare-cell/occupancy machinery. The present theorem instead tests constancy of a continuous-design CATE by variance separation under Hölder propensity, baseline, and effect geometry, bounded observed outcomes, and a higher-order product correction, so neither result is a specialization of the other. Dhawan, Guo and Shah (2026) give a hunted-direction first-order score test; after the proved projection translation, their CATE energy is overlap-equivalent to \(V(P)\), but their power claim still requires their regularity predicate, a conditional direction-correlation lower bound, a conditional score-variance condition, and the corresponding signal scaling. Yu (2026) directly studies CATE variance, but its guarantee retains separate learner-rate conditions, a root-\(n\) ATE condition, boundary nondegeneracy, and its own fold and moment conditions. Thus both are procedure-level power comparators, not uniform full-class minimax converses. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins and Wasserman (2024) provide related nuisance-elbow geometry for pointwise CATE estimation, while Kotekal and Kundu (2025) prove sharp rough-mean heteroskedasticity-testing rates under a different experiment. Crump, Hotz, Imbens and Mitnik (2008), Dai, Shen and Stern (2023), Comminges and Dalalyan (2013), Ingster and Sapatinas (2009), Luedtke, Carone and van der Laan (2019), Lundborg, Kim, Shah and Samworth (2024), Dukes, Stensrud, Brioschi and Hudson (2024), and Sánchez-Becerra (2023) supply complementary testing, quadratic-statistic, or inference results without the present full-class bracket and exact no-penalty phase.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The remaining technical limitation is the absence, when \(\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), of a matching legal observational converse over the unchanged observed-law image. In particular, no verified nuisance-scale prior both preserves constant CATE in every null draw and controls the complete four-cell likelihood through the fixed-design transition regions while respecting the separate propensity, baseline, and CATE Hölder constraints. The coefficient covariance, uniform profiling control, projection constants, and computable basis-dependent constants used by the upper theorem are already proved and are not open limitations.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The statistical class remains exactly the observed image \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) of full causal laws with exact uniform design, outcomes in \([0,1]\), fixed overlap, separate Hölder restrictions on \(e^{\mathrm F}\), \(\mu_0^{\mathrm F}\), and \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\), consistency, and conditional exchangeability. No interior arm-mean band, conditional-variance floor, fitted-nuisance rate, or favorable-direction condition is imposed. The proved claim is the full-class bracket and the exact no-penalty phase \(\alpha+\beta\ge2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), including equality without logarithmic loss. Only the strict rough regime is unresolved: sharpness of \(r_{\mathrm{nu}}\), possible separate \(\alpha\)- and \(\beta\)-elbows, and possible logarithms at further rough-regime boundaries. Unknown design density, smoothness adaptation, and outcomes outside \([0,1]\) remain outside scope. Yu and Dhawan--Guo--Shah are discussed only on intersections satisfying their additional published applicability conditions and do not furnish a uniform converse for this full class.

statement_notes.justification: This is the paper's headline statistical result: it combines a full-class oracle lower endpoint with a uniformly attained higher-order upper endpoint and proves the exact no-penalty phase, including equality without logarithmic loss.
statement_notes.gap: The closest accepted local result, \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier/v1}\), \(\texttt{thm:two-sided-minimax-bracket-all-d}\), concerns scalar-ATE estimation in a discrete arbitrary-cell-mass experiment with a known heterogeneity radius and rare-cell/occupancy machinery. It does not test continuous-design CATE constancy under Hölder propensity, baseline, and effect geometry or analyze the higher-order product correction used here. Yu and Dhawan--Guo--Shah are closer in estimand or procedure, but their results are conditional first-order power guarantees rather than uniform full-class minimax brackets.
